1	# Landing Page - notes
2	
3	Prelude's home page (`/`), today `server/views/_home.eta`: an "Open a project"
4	form and a list of recent projects (name and path only). This design turns it
5	into a dashboard across the person's projects: "what needs me, and where was I?"
6	
7	Pages: `/` (Home), `/loading` (Home before its regions load; the design's way
8	to show it, not a URL the app needs), `/open` (the modal). States: typical,
9	first run (no projects), all caught up, long names.
10	
11	## Decisions
12	
13	- **Across projects** (the person's decision, 2026-10-16). Each project's own
14	  page keeps its full "In progress"; home gathers the parts that need action.
15	- **Needs you includes finished turns and questions** (the person, 2026-10-16),
16	  beside "ready to build", "build stopped" and "pull request open". Each row
17	  links to where it's answered; a pull request opens on the Git server.
18	  What's running right now stays in the bar, not repeated here.
19	- **Projects as a grid of cards** (a handful, the person said): each with its
20	  in-progress designs as links, how many things are waiting on you, and a line
21	  of facts (designs, stack, last change).
22	- **Regions load separately, with skeletons** (the person asked for loading
23	  states). The page arrives with the recent list (cheap); Needs you
24	  (`/home/needs-you`) and the projects' contents (`/home/projects`) each load
25	  into their own region. The projects show their real names and paths at once,
26	  with skeletons only for what's unknown. Each region shows a retry if it
27	  can't be reached. Added `.skeleton` to the design system for it.
28	- **Open a project is a modal** (`/open`), from the Projects heading, or as the

1	# Home named in the window title
2	
3	For anyone with Prelude open next to other windows or tabs. Today the home page's window is called just "Prelude", the same as every other Prelude page, so in the taskbar, the tab strip or the browser's history you can't tell it's Home. Naming it "Home" lets people find their way back to the page that shows what needs them.
4	
5	## What changes
6	
7	- The window (or browser tab) showing the home page is called "Home" instead of "Prelude".
8	- This is true however Home looks: with projects listed, on first run with no projects yet, when nothing is waiting, and when project names and paths are long.
9	- Nothing on the page itself changes: the heading, Needs you, the project cards and Open a project stay as they are.
10	
11	## Acceptance criteria
12	
13	- Going to the home page with projects open, the window's title reads "Home".
14	- On first run, with no projects yet, the window's title reads "Home".
15	- When nothing needs the person, the window's title still reads "Home".
16	- With very long project names and paths, the window's title still reads "Home", and the page looks as it does today.
17	- Coming back to Home from a project's page, the window's title changes back to "Home".
18	- After removing a project whose folder has gone, Home's window title still reads "Home".
19	
20	## Looks right in
21	
22	- **Typical**: `prelude/landing-page/snapshots/typical/index.html`
23	- **First run**: `prelude/landing-page/snapshots/first-run/index.html`
24	- **All caught up**: `prelude/landing-page/snapshots/all-caught-up/index.html`
25	- **Long names**: `prelude/landing-page/snapshots/long-names/index.html`
26	
27	## For developers
28	
29	- Route `/` → view `@app/server/views/home/index` (`server/views/home/index.eta`, which includes `home/_home.eta`), titled "Home" in `routes.json`. The body, regions and styles already match the approved screens; only `<title>` differs.

1	// Design branches (plan: step 9).
2	//
3	// In a git repository every design works on a branch of its own,
4	// prelude/<design>, in a git worktree under <home>/worktrees/: its design
5	// sessions and its build sessions both work there, every turn is committed,
6	// and the branch is merged once - design and code together. Prelude never
7	// writes to the person's own checkout; it changes only when a branch is
8	// merged into it locally.
9	//
10	// Prelude treats a worktree as a folder of its own - its own design origin,
11	// design host and check - so everything that works for a folder works for a
12	// design's branch, and the sessions' transcripts merge with the branch.
13	//
14	// Which worktrees exist is a machine-local convenience, kept in
15	// <home>/builds.json (ground rule 1): the branch is what matters, and it's in
16	// git. Once a branch that did some work is in the main branch - merged here,
17	// or by a pull request on the server - its worktree and branch are removed,
18	// and the folder says so.
19

29	// worktree starts a daemon that outlives it, and can hold this process's
30	// pipes open.

I've made R-c7w true: Prelude's branch worktrees no longer show up as projects of their own. I couldn't run anything here, so the new test and the rest of the checks haven't run yet. Prelude's render after this turn is the first check.

The views, states and routes didn't need to change; this was all server code.

**What I changed**
- **`server/folders.js`**: any folder under `~/.prelude/worktrees/` now counts as a design's worktree.
  - When the recent list is read, any record of one is removed from `folders.json`, whether its folder is gone or still there. That clears out the records already in the list, including the "gone" cards left behind by merged branches.
  - `open()` never adds a worktree to the list.
- **`server/branches.js`**: added `repositoryOf(path)`, which finds the repository a worktree belongs to.
- **`server/main.js`**:
  - **Opening a worktree directly** (`POST /folders` with its path) opens its project instead, so the person lands on the project page and the branch's work shows in that project's card.
  - **If git no longer knows the worktree**, so its project can't be found, the Open dialog refuses it with a 422 and an error message. That message is new wording, not taken from the design.
  - **Visiting a worktree's own page** no longer adds it to the list. That was how these records kept getting in.
- **`test/home.test.js`**: a new test covering all three: old worktree records are dropped, and a worktree git doesn't know is refused and not listed.
- **`RULES.md`**: removed R-c7w's *proposed* line, nothing else.
- **`NOTES.md`**: added what was built under "Projects, only projects".

The story (`home/1`, the window title) doesn't touch this change; it was already built, and nothing here affects the title.

**Before approving and opening the pull request**
- **Your own project list**: the first time Home loads, your `~/.prelude/folders.json` will lose its worktree entries. Only the real projects should stay, with their branch work showing in their cards.
- **The existing build test**: `test/build.test.js:342` opens a worktree "as a plain folder". It still passes, but that now opens the project, so the comment above it describes the old behaviour.
- **The refusal wording**: check you're happy with it, since the design doesn't cover that case.
